notes: Sweep 2026-10-23 at head d04061d (uncommitted false in every result.json): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier, and every assistant message in each transcript comes from that model. No transcript has a Skill tool call (the two "name":"Skill" hits per transcript are the tool definition) or any SKILL.md text, and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line requires. All five added tests. Every result.json records skills_listed 209, where the 2026-10-22-d sessions were shown 16 or 29 skills.

Rules changed since ba24972 (git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/): SKILL.md adds three paragraphs to "Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern..." and rewrites "In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use"; ex_unit.md adds one sentence to "Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler". None of the seven rules this case grades changed, so all seven are graded to the 2026-10-22-d standard and no verdict here is decided by a new sentence. The per-bullet counts asked for the rewritten rules belong to the webhook-parser and library-client grades; shop-project's case file has no such bullets and the index does not list either rewritten rule for this case. Neither rewritten rule is broken in these outputs: no function here reads a required key with map[:key], and the one multi-clause function that binds a field in its head is opus-1's total/2 (line 87 binds `items` for its map_size guard).

Before you finish (unchanged since ba24972): step 1 is met by a project-wide mix format or a passing mix format --check-formatted after the last edit, as in 2026-10-22-d; a mix test that compiles the app stands in for step 2; step 3 (mix credo --strict) is required since the project has Credo. Opus-1 ran "mix format && mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force 2>&1 | tail -20 && mix test 2>&1 | tail -20 && mix credo --strict 2>&1 | tail -15" (#7) after its last edit, the first baseline run in the last two sweeps with a separate compile, and is clean. The other four never ran Credo and break step 3: haiku-1 and haiku-2 ran mix test then mix format --check-formatted (passed); sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 ran "mix format && mix test 2>&1 | tail -8". Result: 4 of 5 violated, the same split as 2026-10-22-d (opus clean, both Haiku and both Sonnet violated). Sonnet-2 now meets step 1, where in 2026-10-22-d it never formatted.

The case's per-file formatting check line is missed in 5 of 5, as in 2026-10-22-d: every run wrote lib/shop/cart.ex, then edited test/shop/cart_test.exs, before any format or check, and formatted or checked once, project-wide, at the end. Replay: every Write and Edit applied in order to the case's shop-project files gives files byte-identical to each run's final files, so the end-of-run formatter changed nothing in any run.

What each session ran after its edits (#n counts unique tool calls). opus-1: #7 format, compile --warnings-as-errors --force ("Compiling 1 file (.ex) / Generated shop app", no warnings), test (16 passed), credo --strict (no issues). haiku-1: #8 mix test 2>&1 (no warnings, 17 passed), #9 mix format --check-formatted (no output). haiku-2: #10 mix test 2>&1 (no warnings, 16 passed), #12 mix format --check-formatted (no output). sonnet-1: #5 mix format && mix test 2>&1 | tail -8 (no warnings, 15 passed). sonnet-2: #7 the same command (no warnings, 14 passed).

Refused commands (only commands starting with mix, elixir or elixirc were pre-approved). haiku-1 #7 and haiku-2 #9 chained mix test with echo and a format check; haiku-2 #1 was a find -exec listing and #11 a format check with echo; each was re-run as plain commands. Sonnet-1 #2 and sonnet-2 #3 were python3 heredoc edits chained with "mix format && mix test 2>&1"; both sessions then made the change with Write or Edit. Sonnet-2 #2 called a tool named bash_placeholder that does not exist. No refused command carried mix credo --strict, so no refusal changes a Before you finish verdict.

Chain fallible steps with `with` (unchanged since ba24972): sonnet-1 writes two one-step withs in public functions whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result, apply_code/2 (lines 67-71) and total/2 (lines 87-91), the shape "This holds in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result" names. The other four write no with: opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-2 handle their one fallible lookup with case and haiku-2 uses if on a membership test, which the 2026-10-22-d standard grades not exercised. One-step with: 1 of 5 runs (1 of 5 in 2026-10-22-d, then opus-1).

Update structs (unchanged): the defstruct sentence decides all five, as in 2026-10-22-d. opus-1 line 7, sonnet-1 line 9 and sonnet-2 line 9 `defstruct [:items, discount: nil]`; haiku-1 line 9 and haiku-2 line 10 `defstruct [:items, discount_code: nil]`. 5 of 5, as before. All five follow the update-syntax sentences; Map.put/3 or Map.delete/2 on the inner items map inside %{cart | items: ...} is not the pattern the rule forbids.

Other unchanged rules, graded to the 2026-10-22-d standard. Return tuples: a total that raises KeyError on an unpriced SKU counts as clean when its @doc names the KeyError, which opus-1 (lines 81-82), haiku-1 (line 75), haiku-2 (line 64) and sonnet-2 (lines 76-77) do; sonnet-1's total/2 returns {:error, {:missing_price, sku}} instead, the first baseline run in two sweeps to do so. Atoms: opus-1 and haiku-1 map trimmed, upcased codes through a literal map with Map.fetch/2; haiku-2 keeps the normalized string checked against a literal list; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use one parse_code/1 clause per string. All clean. Naming: haiku-1's `input` (line 55) is counted as a role name and the bare `_ ->` clauses (opus-1 line 42, sonnet-1 lines 46 and 97) are not counted, as before. Money: all five use integer div; opus-1 rounds the discount to the nearest cent (div(subtotal + 5, 10), 155 with SAVE10 gives 638), the other four round down (639).

Verified in scratch copies of each run's project (lib, test, mix.exs, mix.lock, .formatter.exs; deps from one mix deps.get). mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors and mix test pass in all five (opus-1 16 tests, haiku-1 17, haiku-2 16, sonnet-1 15, sonnet-2 14), and result.json records mix credo --strict with no issues in all five. A mix run probe with 2 x APPLE at 100 gives 699, 679 with SAVE10 and 200 with FREESHIP in all five, as bare integers except sonnet-1's {:ok, 699}, {:ok, 679}, {:ok, 200}. BOGUS returns {:error, :unknown_code} in all five. A second code is rejected by opus-1 ({:error, :discount_already_applied}) and both Sonnet runs ({:error, :code_already_applied}) and replaces the first in both Haiku runs. " save10 " is accepted by opus-1 and both Haiku runs. Removing 5 of 2 units empties the items, 1 of 2 leaves 1, and an absent SKU leaves the cart unchanged in all five. An empty cart totals 0 in opus-1 (documented at line 84) and 499 in the others. No lib file has String.to_atom/1, String.to_existing_atom/1 or a float.

other_violations follows the 2026-10-22-d grades: Enum.reduce sums where Enum.sum_by/2 fits (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-2; sonnet-1's reduce_while halts on a missing price and is not a plain sum); multi-step pipelines on one line, in lib (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2) and in tests (sonnet-1, sonnet-2); bare `{:ok, cart} = ...` arrange matches and bind-then-== under Assert with patterns (all five).
